question: A hemisphere is melted and recast into a cone of the same radius R. Find the height of the cone formed.
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

When a solid is melted and recast into another shape, their volumes remain equal.

Volume of Hemisphere = Volume of Cone

⇒ ²/₃ × π × R³ = ¹/₃ × π × R² × h

⇒ 2 × R = h

**∴ The correct answer is 2R.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Radius of the hemisphere = R

Radius of the recast cone = R

**Formula Used:**

Volume of a hemisphere = ²/₃ × π × r³

Volume of a cone = ¹/₃ × π × r² × h

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let the height of the newly formed cone be h.

⇒ Since the hemisphere is simply melted to form the cone, the original material volume completely transforms into the new volume.

⇒ Volume of Hemisphere = Volume of Cone

⇒ ²/₃ × π × R³ = ¹/₃ × π × R² × h

⇒ Canceling the common terms (¹/₃ and π) from both sides:

⇒ 2 × R³ = R² × h

⇒ Dividing both sides by R²:

⇒ h = 2R

**∴ The correct answer is 2R.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Melting and Recasting Property

When any 3D solid is melted and recast into another shape, the total volume of the material remains strictly constant, even though dimensions and total surface area typically change.

Volume Relation of Cylinder & Cone

For a given identical radius (r) and height (h), the volume of a cylinder (V = πr²h) is exactly 3 times the volume of a cone (V = ¹/₃πr²h).

Hemisphere Surface Areas

The Curved Surface Area (CSA) of a solid hemisphere is 2πr², while its Total Surface Area (TSA) includes the flat circular base, resulting in 3πr².
